newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Fujian Enterprises loan upped to US$70 mln.
newsitem.headline: China's Fujian Enterprises loan upped to US$70 mln.

text.p: Fujian Enterprises (Holdings) Co's four-year transferable loan facility has been increased to US$70 million from US$40 million because of oversubscription, said arranger Standard Chartered Investment Banking on Friday.

The borrower, which is wholly owned by and under the jurisdiction of the Fujian Provincial People's Government, was established in Hong Kong in 1980. It is engaged in trading, transportation, tourism, real estate, financial services and shipping.

The loan has an average life of 2.175 years and pays a margin of 137.5 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return for top tier managers is 211.1 basis points.
Arrangers, with US$5 million each, are Standard Chartered Investment Banking, AB Capital Markets (HK), KMBC Asia and KEXIM Asia.
Co-lead managers, with US$5 million each, are Bank of Nova Scotia's Guangzhou Branch, Industrial Bank of Korea's Hongkong Branch, Kincheng-Tokyo Finance and Union Bank of Hong Kong.

Managers are ABN AMRO Bank's Hong Kong Branch, Asia Commercial Bank, Deutsche Bank's Hong Kong Branch, Development Bank of Singapore's Shanghai Branch, Hong Kong Chinese Bank, Kookmin Finance Asia, Shanghai International Finance Co and Wing Lung Bank, with US$3 million each, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia's Hong Kong Branch, Korea Industrial Leasing Co (Hong Kong) and Mitsui Leasing & Development (Hong Kong) Co, with US$2 million each.
